metrics.name: pause_length
metrics.threshold: >= 0.3 s longer than reference, mid-phrase (no punctuation)

regions.explanation: At 23.41s, between “tides” and “of”, a 810 ms silence replaced the reference's 0 ms pause. A long silence where the reference has none - especially mid-phrase - breaks the syntactic unit and signals lost place rather than deliberate emphasis. Fix: Keep this phrase in one breath; pause at the punctuation instead.

regions.text: prosperity and the still waters of peace. Yet, every so often the oath is
regions.explanation: From 24.41s to 28.88s (“prosperity and the still waters of peace. Yet, every so …”), 3 pause(s) at punctuation shrank from 447 ms to 0 ms on average. Pauses at punctuation mark the end of an idea and give the audience time to absorb it; running through them merges separate thoughts into one stream. Fix: Hold a clear pause at each punctuation mark, about as long as the reference.

From 29.40s to 30.82s (“gathering clouds and raging storms.”), loudness relative to the speaker's own level fell 7.1 dB below the reference, bottoming out 10.6 dB down; that is 1.9× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. The loudness falls away across the phrase, so its final words - often the payoff - drop toward the noise floor of the room. Fix: Support the breath through the end of the phrase; the last words need the same energy as the first.

regions.text: or vision of those in high office,
regions.explanation: From 35.65s to 38.43s (“or vision of those in high office,”), articulation rate slowed to 3.70 syll/s against 6.57 syll/s in the reference (-44%); that is 2.9× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Stretched words without matching emphasis read as hesitation and dilute the rhythm of the phrase; the audience's attention drifts between content words. Fix: Tighten these words to the reference pace; keep length only on the stressed word.
